George Russell wins the Zandvoort Sprint for Mercedes.

Antonelli finished 4th after floor damage in qualifying yesterday — his championship lead is now just 56 points.

Race day tomorrow. Qualifying still ahead. Game on. 🍿

#F1 #DutchGP #Formula1

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM ET

George Russell won the Dutch Grand Prix sprint race at Zandvoort. 🏁

The Mercedes driver converted his pole position into a commanding victory, beating Charles Leclerc's Ferrari in second and Lando Norris's McLaren in third.

The big story coming out of the sprint: championship leader Kimi Antonelli finished fourth. He had his Mercedes floor damaged in sprint qualifying the day before — that cost him pace throughout today's sprint, and the points he gave up are exactly the kind the Antonelli camp didn't want to donate.

Here's where the championship stands after the sprint: Russell has closed to within 56 points of Antonelli. With 316 points still up for grabs in the 2026 season, that gap is absolutely closable.

Oscar Piastri was fifth in the sprint. Home hero Max Verstappen — racing at Zandvoort for what may be his final time in this track's last-ever Dutch GP — finished sixth in front of a roaring Orange Army.

Sprint wins are four points for the winner. They're not going to decide the championship on their own. But they matter. And Russell took his today.

The real prize comes Sunday. First: qualifying. Then: the race. Stay tuned. 🍿

article.headline: Russell Wins Dutch GP Sprint, Closes to 56 Points Behind Championship Leader Antonelli

The Dutch GP brought orange armies, Verstappen dominance, and some of the best atmospheres in modern F1.

This weekend, it all ends. 🧡

#F1 #DutchGP #Zandvoort

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Zandvoort has hosted some of the loudest, most passionate F1 crowds in history.

2026: the final chapter. Orange Army, one last time.

Tomorrow's race ends a 5-year F1 run that nobody expected to be this good.

#F1 #DutchGP #Zandvoort

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:00 AM ET

Tomorrow is the last F1 race Zandvoort will ever host.

The Dutch Grand Prix returns to the F1 calendar in 2021 during a wave of Verstappen-fueled national pride, and what followed was one of the greatest home-crowd runs in modern motorsport history. Max Verstappen won five consecutive Dutch Grand Prix races. The Orange Army — 100,000+ fans dressed head-to-toe in orange — turned Zandvoort into an experience unlike any other on the calendar.

In 2026, the Dutch GP has been dropped from the F1 schedule. This weekend is the farewell. One last sprint format. One last qualifying session. One last race.

And now, on Saturday August 22, after the Sprint race has been run and qualifying is finished, we're one sleep away from the final Dutch Grand Prix.

Verstappen is racing in his last home race — ever. At least at this circuit. The man whose popularity brought Zandvoort back to Formula 1 will close the loop tomorrow.

If you've never felt the power of the Orange Army, spend time watching the crowd shots during Sunday's broadcast. It is something special.

This is how it ends. Not with a whimper — with a 72-lap championship-implications title fight at one of the most unique, atmospheric circuits in the world.

Goodbye, Zandvoort. You were magnificent. 🧡

article.headline: Goodbye, Zandvoort: The Final Dutch Grand Prix and the End of an Orange Era

stories.title: Hadjar Wrist Injury — Lawson Returns to Red Bull for Dutch GP — Tier 2

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Isack Hadjar won't race in the Dutch GP.

A wrist injury from boxing during summer break has him sidelined. Liam Lawson is back in the Red Bull seat.

Tsunoda returns to Racing Bulls. Lineup musical chairs at the worst time.

#F1 #DutchGP #RedBull

facebook.long_form:
Window: 12:00 PM ET

This is not how Isack Hadjar planned his summer.

The Red Bull driver — who took the senior seat at the start of 2026, displacing Yuki Tsunoda — picked up a wrist injury during summer break while boxing at the gym. The injury is bad enough that he's been ruled out of this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort.

In his place: Liam Lawson is back. The 24-year-old New Zealander stepped up to Red Bull as reserve driver and has now been confirmed for the Dutch GP race seat. Lawson actually made his F1 debut at the 2023 Dutch Grand Prix — so there's a neat full-circle element to his return at this circuit.

The driver musical chairs cascade further: with Lawson moving to Red Bull, Yuki Tsunoda has returned to Racing Bulls alongside Arvid Lindblad — somewhat ironic, given that Tsunoda was the one displaced by Hadjar when the season started.

Neither Lawson nor Tsunoda made it through SQ2 in sprint qualifying (Lawson P11, Tsunoda P12), so both start deep in the sprint grid.

It's a strange situation at both Red Bull teams this weekend. But F1 never runs out of storylines.

Get well soon, Isack. 🙏

article.headline: Hadjar's Boxing Injury Brings Lawson Back to Red Bull — and Tsunoda Back to Racing Bulls

F1 Championship after Dutch GP Sprint:

Antonelli: leads
Russell: 56 points behind
Hamilton: chasing

316 points still available. Today's qualifying + tomorrow's race could flip everything.

This title fight isn't going to slow down. 🏆

#F1 #Formula1 #DutchGP

facebook.long_form:
Window: 2:00 PM ET

Let's talk about the F1 championship picture after today's Zandvoort sprint.

Kimi Antonelli came into this weekend with a healthy lead. He's won six races this season. He's had six pole positions. He's been consistent, fast, and composed under enormous pressure as a 20-year-old fighting for the world championship.

Today, he finished fourth in the sprint. Not a disaster — but not what he needed after damaging his car's floor in qualifying.

George Russell won the sprint. The points gap between them is now 56. That sounds comfortable — until you realize 316 points are still available in the 2026 season, and Russell is having the best second half of any season in his career.

Lewis Hamilton sits in third in the championship, around 169 points, unlikely to win it but capable of playing spoiler in key races — perhaps even this weekend at Zandvoort.

The title fight in 2026 is between two Mercedes teammates. One young and hungry, one experienced and desperate. Both fast. It's remarkable.

Today's sprint was one data point. Tomorrow's race is the real thing. Watch the first lap closely — championship battles in F1 are often decided by who blinks first in the opening corners.

Antonelli hasn't blinked yet. But Russell is getting closer. 👀

article.headline: Championship Watch: Antonelli's Lead Trimmed to 56 Points as Russell Wins Dutch GP Sprint

Don't miss it. The final Dutch GP. 🇳🇱

#F1 #DutchGP #Zandvoort

facebook.long_form:
Window: 5:00 PM ET

Everything you need to know for Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort. 🇳🇱

**Race start:** Sunday, August 23 at 15:00 CEST (9:00 AM ET)
**Laps:** 72 around Circuit Zandvoort
**The big fact:** It's the LAST-EVER Dutch Grand Prix at this circuit

**Three storylines to watch:**

**1. Antonelli vs. Russell — title implications**
Russell won today's sprint. If he wins tomorrow from the front and Antonelli has another difficult race, this championship tightens significantly. Antonelli needs a strong qualifying position and a clean race to reassert control.

**2. Verstappen's last home race**
Max Verstappen is racing at Zandvoort for the final time. The Dutch GP was essentially built around his popularity — it came back to the calendar in 2021 because the Netherlands had a world champion. He's won here five times. Tomorrow could be his last chance for No. 6, and the Orange Army wants it badly.

**3. Weather wildcard**
Rain is in the forecast for Sunday. Wet conditions at Zandvoort — with its banked turns, tight sector two, and flowing final sector — create genuine strategic chaos. If it rains, anything can happen.

Set your alarms. 🍿
